target_customer: Manufacturing and logistics operators that want robot labor without buying robots
problem: Robots are expensive and hard to deploy. Eden offers semi-humanoid robots as a usage-priced service so firms pay per hour.
business_model: Robots as a service, usage-based, listed from $10 per hour with no setup fee
product_category: Robots-as-a-service and robot operating software (Theta OS)

founders.name: Stamatios Floratos
previous_startups: Bootstrapped a seven-figure B2B adtech company working with influencers, started at age 13 (per YC bio)

founders.name: Joseph Humphreys
founders.background_notes: YC bio cites a Nature publication and work on many robot morphologies.

competitors.name: Formic
competitors.what: Robotics as a service for manufacturers
competitors.funding_then: Raised $50M Series B per The Next Web

competitors.name: Figure
competitors.what: Humanoids at BMW reported at $25 per robot operating hour

competitors.name: Agility Robotics
competitors.what: Digit humanoid sold as a service at roughly $10 to $30 per hour per secondary sources

technical_complexity.rationale: General-purpose semi-humanoid manipulation that works out of the box is research-grade for a four person team.

defensibility.rationale: Funded humanoid and RaaS players already price per hour. Fleet data and operating software could build lock-in but no evidence yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to say; first YC batch.

market_need_then: 2026 sources describe pilot humanoid deployments at automakers priced per hour, indicating a market for usage-priced robot labor.

branding.domain_note: Uses edenrobotics.ai; the .com is not confirmed.

identity.logo: Logo exists, design not described by sources
identity.visual_style: Industrial product page with Theta OS branding
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and slogan driven: One Robot. Every Industry.

brand_strength.rationale: Search results mix this company with several other firms named Eden, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Eden Robotics is an Active Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. It is pre-product by one analyst page and sells robots as a service in a field where funded humanoid firms already offer per-hour pricing. Technical difficulty is very high for a four person team.
notes: Unverified: one listing site reports $500K total raised at seed; no primary source. Other funding hits for companies named Eden belong to different companies. Founder employers and schools were not found. Competitor items are 2026 secondary sources, not launch coverage of Eden's own date.
